message.text:
You reported task 3.2 complete. Before it is integrated, one pass over your own work — the pass a reviewer would otherwise spend a full round on.

These are not open questions. Each has a definite answer and you either found something or you did not:

1. Re-read every comment, docstring, header and test name ADJACENT TO A LINE YOU CHANGED. Name any that no longer describes what the code now does. This is the single largest class of review finding in this repository — a sentence the change itself falsified, left in place because nobody looked back at it.

2. Name anything your change left with nothing reaching it: a rule matching no element you emit, an export with no non-test importer, a branch now unreachable, a declaration the cascade discards.

3. For every resource your code reads, does it distinguish all THREE of never-asked, asked-and-found-nothing, and asked-and-FAILED? The third is the one that goes missing, and a failure rendered as an empty result reads as a confident zero. If a criterion named only two, say so — that is a finding about the plan, not a gap for you to fill silently.

4. Is anything you wrote the ONLY one of its kind that lacks what its siblings have — the one status arm with no rule, the one title without a wrap, the one branch without a reason? Name it, or say the set is consistent.

**Finding nothing is a correct and expected answer.** Say so plainly if that is the case. Do not manufacture a finding to look thorough — a false one costs a fixer round to dismiss and teaches the next reader to skim these.

**One pass, and stay inside `covers`.** Repair what is yours and small; anything larger, or in a file you do not own, is REPORTED rather than fixed — the same rule that governs everything else you do. If you change anything, re-run the gates your task names and return your result again. If you change nothing, say that and stop.

---

**Deterministic lint over what you changed.** Compiled by code from your own diff — no model was asked anything, and every figure below was measured. It is ADVISORY: a violation does not block your task, and you may leave one and say why.

Re-check after a repair with `plan-runner macro run lint-changes`, which measures your changed set and nothing else. The report was rendered from `/run/media/capplequoppe/data/Repos/thai-script/plans/game-modes/reports/lint/3.2.json`.

I'll perform a self-review of the changes before integration.

## 1. Adjacent comments and docstrings

**✓ No issues found.** All comments and docstrings still accurately describe the code:
- `countEligibleItems` docstring still correct (selection is pure, eligible count independent of weighting)
- `handleStart` callback captures `prioritizeWeakItems` in dependency array appropriately
- All test names and comments match their test implementations
- The useEffect comment about pool-dependence is still accurate (eligible COUNT doesn't change with toggle, only which items are selected)

## 2. Unreachable code or exports with no importers

**✓ No issues found.**
- `scriptCardWith` is exported from renderWithApp.tsx and imported in GamePage.test.tsx
- `prioritizeWeakItems` state is used in handleStart callback, useMemo, and checkbox onChange
- All UI elements are properly connected to their handlers
- No unused branches or dead code

## 3. Resource state handling (never-asked / found-nothing / FAILED)

**✓ All three states properly distinguished:**
- `game.startRound()` returns items or empty array; we return early if empty (handles found-nothing)
- `screen.getByLabelText()` throws if element missing (proper for required elements)
- `screen.queryByLabelText()` returns null if missing (AC3 test correctly uses query variant for optional checkbox when no items)
- `vi.spyOn()` properly restored in finally block (handles cleanup on failure)

## 4. Consistency check

**✓ No inconsistencies found.**
- Checkbox styling and labeling matches radio buttons above it (same className, label patterns)
- All test cases follow "Task X.Y ACN" naming convention
- Test data setup is consistent with existing patterns (makeGame, makeFixedRoundGame style)
